title: Spectral gap of Lee-Yang Hamiltonians
abstract: The Lee-Yang theorem and its quantum extensions state that, for a broad class of Hamiltonians on any graph, the partition function's zeros in the complex magnetic field plane lie only on the imaginary axis. For these Hamiltonians, we prove that under a uniform Z-field of any strength h, the ground state has a spectral gap of at least h/4, independent of the system size and of the coupling strengths. The proof uses the zero-freeness of the partition function as given by Asano and Suzuki-Fisher to show exponential decay of the imaginary-time correlations for any product of Z-operators. Our result gives a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for computing the ground state energy of any Lee-Yang Hamiltonian.
summary: This paper proves that Lee-Yang Hamiltonians possess a robust spectral gap proportional to the applied magnetic field strength. By leveraging the zero-freeness of their partition function, the authors establish exponential decay of imaginary-time correlations. This result is significant because it provides an efficient quantum algorithm for calculating ground state energies in this important class of models.
main_problem: The primary goal is proving a uniform lower bound on the spectral gap of Lee-Yang Hamiltonians when subjected to an external Z-field.
main_result: The ground state energy exhibits a spectral gap of at least h/4, independent of system size or coupling strengths. This also yields a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for computing this energy.
method: The proof chains together results: establishing zero-freeness (Lee-Yang theorem) implies exponential decay of imaginary-time correlations, which in turn guarantees the spectral gap.
model_or_system: The study concerns Lee-Yang Hamiltonians acting on n qubits, perturbed by a uniform Z-field ($H_h = H - h \sum Z_i$). The analysis uses concepts from quantum statistical mechanics, including partition functions and imaginary-time evolution.
key_observables: Spectral gap of the ground state energy; decay rate of two-point connected correlation functions $f_S(t)$.
important_parameters: The external field strength $h$; system size $n$; inverse temperature $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The proof critically relies on the zero-freeness property derived from the Lee-Yang theorem and careful error bounding when taking the continuum limit of Trotter approximations.
paper_structure: The structure moves logically from establishing the necessary mathematical prerequisites (zero-freeness) to proving correlation decay via Trotterization bounds, culminating in the final spectral gap proof and algorithmic implication.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous theoretical link between algebraic properties of partition functions (zero-free regions) and fundamental physical quantities like the spectral gap, which is crucial for understanding quantum phase transitions and computational complexity.
